generation.hypothesis: Applying a single high-pressure, high-temperature treatment to homogenized Al0.7CoCrFeNi will replace its crack-prone lamellar architecture with a coherent hierarchical pattern, thereby approximately doubling both room-temperature tensile strength and ductility rather than trading one property for the other.
generation.material_initial_state: The study will start from homogenized eutectic Al0.7CoCrFeNi containing dual-phase FCC/B2 lamellar colonies. The softer FCC and harder B2 phases will initially be separated by largely incoherent internal interfaces, where dislocation pile-ups would promote local stress concentrations, interfacial microcracking, and brittle failure.
generation.intervention: The alloy will receive one high-pressure and high-temperature treatment in the solid state, followed by cooling and decompression.
generation.conditions: Treatment will be conducted at approximately 6 GPa and 1470 K. Mechanical performance will be evaluated under room-temperature uniaxial tension, including interrupted testing to strains approaching 35%.
generation.structural_mediator: The treatment is expected to transform the dual-phase lamellae into a hierarchically patterned FCC/B2 microstructure with coherent interfaces while preserving the two-phase architecture.
generation.mechanism: Coherent interfaces should permit preferential transfer of dislocations from the softer FCC phase into the harder B2 phase, reducing pile-ups and associated stress concentrations. The hierarchical pattern should also activate complementary dislocation slip, stacking faults, microbands, and deformation twins. Together, these processes would distribute strain more uniformly between phases, delay plastic instability, and replace catastrophic interfacial crack propagation with spatially distributed microcracking.
generation.predicted_outcome: The treated alloy should reach a fracture strength of about 1.1-1.2 GPa and a uniform tensile elongation of roughly 35-40% at room temperature. Both properties would be approximately twice those of the untreated alloy, while fracture would shift from elongated interfacial cracks toward isolated, distributed microcracks.
generation.baseline: The comparator will be the untreated homogenized or conventionally cast eutectic alloy, which would retain strong-yet-brittle FCC/B2 lamellae, with strength and elongation roughly half the predicted treated values.
generation.boundary: The synergy is expected only when pressure near 6 GPa at about 1470 K induces the coherent hierarchical pattern. Similar-temperature hot isostatic pressing or thermomechanical treatment at substantially lower pressure should not provide the same combined improvement.
generation.uncertainty: The principal uncertainty is whether pressure-temperature processing will reproducibly create sufficient interfacial coherence throughout the bulk alloy to enable phase-to-phase dislocation transfer.

falsification_experiment.design: Compare untreated and high-pressure-treated specimens in room-temperature tensile tests, including interruption near 35% strain and post-fracture microstructural examination.
measurements: Fracture strength and uniform tensile elongation
FCC- and B2-phase geometrically necessary dislocation densities by EBSD
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis will be falsified if treatment fails to produce approximately 1.1 GPa strength with about 35% elongation, or if phase-specific dislocation densities do not converge near 35% strain and elongated interfacial cracks remain dominant.
